As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for completely banning students from using their phones throughout the entire school day.

As the new school year starts, support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to rise

Yes, although it is still July, summer vacation has somehow already ended for some reason. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow — for the second consecutive summer, the first day of the new school year has not fallen in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion, where eligible students and educators can receive a gift card of up to US$150 when they purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27. Consumers in several states can also benefit from limited-time sales tax holidays.

Although back-to-school discounts are welcome news, smartphone use during class time is becoming increasingly unpopular.

Popular comments from GreenPizza

I haven't seen any data supporting the idea that student phone use reduces the risk of school shootings. The reality is that reducing distractions during class time is the only way to truly fulfill the original purpose of going to school.

A recent survey by the Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using their phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for a stricter, all-day ban covering the entire period from class time to dismissal has risen even more significantly. For the first time, more Americans support rather than oppose a complete ban on phone use throughout the entire school day.

The report also noted that although support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger generations remain more lukewarm in their attitudes toward both classroom bans and all-day bans. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use to class time only, implement an all-day ban from class to dismissal, or leave the decision to students and parents? Share your thoughts in the comments section.
